speaker: Dr Charlene Chen
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) whether the Ministry tracks data on employee burnout by sector; (b) if so, which sectors have the highest levels of employee burnout leading to higher attrition; and (c) how can the Ministry both alleviate pressures in these sectors and channel jobseekers into areas where there is demand for manpower, while ensuring that working conditions remain sustainable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: MOM and the WSH Council are working with tripartite partners to encourage greater adoption of iWorkHealth so that more employers can better understand their employees' state of mental well-being at work and offer relevant support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: While it is natural to feel overwhelmed at work from time to time, a conducive environment can help workers to reduce or overcome work stress.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Launched by the WSH Council, the Well-being Champions Network also facilitates the exchange of best practices among the participating companies and offers access to resources and training to strengthen workplace mental well-being.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Beyond efforts to promote the health and well-being of employees at the workplace, MOM also supports jobseekers in making informed career decisions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Manpower (Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: The tools and resources available can help jobseekers identify and seize opportunities to enter jobs that are more aligned with their aspirations and preferences, so that they can adopt a more sustainable pace of work and avoid the risk of burnout.

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: I ask the question because I have a hunch on certain sectors that might be experiencing burnout and there could be some initiatives to help the sectors.

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: So, I am very glad that there is iWorkHealth, the Well-being Champions Network and the Tripartite Advisory.

speaker: Dr Charlene Chen (Tampines)
text: I wonder if there are any other initiatives that can be targeted at both the employers and the employees to support mental well-being?

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: MOM has worked with a range of partners, such as the WSH Council, to roll out a range of resources to support the companies in strengthening the well-being in the workplace.

speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
text: There are two areas that we can do more.
